GALE
Ingest Docs Source v0.1.0

Open source · Apache-2.0 · v0.1.0

A time-series database for wind-farm telemetry.

Gale ingests millions of turbine sensor readings a second and keeps every one of them queryable — from a single nacelle to a 180-turbine farm.

180 × 420 × 25. Gale is built so that number is the easy part: nothing on the write path waits on a read, a lock, or a random seek.

  1. 01

    Frame

    Each turbine gateway batches 100 ms of readings into one frame on one long-lived stream. No request per point, no ack per point.

    100 ms · ≈1,050 readings per frame

  2. 02

    Log

    Frames append to a write-ahead log in arrival order. One fsync covers every stream that arrived in the same 10 ms window.

    Group commit · 10 ms

  3. 03

    Columns

    Readings land in per-series column buffers in memory. Turbine clocks only move forward, so every append is already in order.

    Per series · append-only · no sort

  4. 04

    Seal

    Full buffers seal into immutable segments: delta-of-delta timestamps, XOR-encoded floats. Queries read segments; writes never touch them.

    Bits per reading · measure it below

Run the codec in this tab.

Stage 04 is the same pair of encoders Gale uses — delta-of-delta for timestamps, XOR for values. This runs them over a synthetic 420-channel turbine stream on one JavaScript thread and counts every bit.
